rationale: B wins because it has better fact discipline. A builds a whole angle on "Monzo re-enters a US challenger-bank market that already has three incumbents" and then names rivals the update never supplied; that is not an angle, it is homework pretending to be copy. B also overreaches with "Monzo's first profitable year is paying for a second shot at America," but it mostly contains the damage by listing the exact proof needed and by refusing "Monzo takes on America's neobanks" for the reason A missed.
gaps_in_A: "Monzo re-enters a US challenger-bank market that already has three incumbents" imports a competitive landscape and a count not in the update.
"Chime, Varo, Current, and similar" names competitors without source support from the supplied facts.
"Monzo is explicitly pairing its first-ever annual profit with a second US run" overstates intent; the set later admits this is only an inference.
"The prevailing assumption...is that a neobank needs its own national charter" needs sourcing before it can carry a contrarian angle.
gaps_in_B: "Monzo's first profitable year is paying for a second shot at America" asserts funding causality the update does not provide.
"a costly overseas expansion" is directionally plausible but unsupported; CAC and US targets are explicitly undisclosed.
"exec-spotlight" is premature without a named US launch executive in the facts.
"draft a single tight pitch" comes too early unless the partner bank, results date, and launch owner can be put on record.
